page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with multithreading on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz. The compute topology is backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced instruction set extensions, including AVX-512, Intel AMX tile and int8, and cryptographic primitives like VAES and SHA-NI to accelerate vector mathematics and secure operations.

The instance provides 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU density tailored for processing tasks that do not demand expansive memory footprints. The machine includes zero local storage disks and no GPU acceleration devices, directing persistent data input and output operations across network-attached block storage infrastructure. Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached read speeds of 52.52 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 32.72 GB/sec, alongside a cached small-block bandwidth of 544.86 GB/sec.

Synthetic and application benchmarks place the c3-highcpu-8 in the middle tier across most standard evaluations. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,628 and a PassMark CPU rating of 11,808.29, supporting static web serving throughput of 13.01 GB/sec and 8.86 million Redis SET operations per second. Throughput drops into the lower quartile for highly parallel compression tasks such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (35.86 GB/sec) and generative text execution on 7B parameter models (7.72 tokens/sec).

Qualitatively, the server provides efficient CPU capacity by trading memory capacity and bundled NVMe storage for dedicated computational execution. This resource profile fits workloads where memory footprint remains moderate, including software compilation, continuous integration build agents, static and dynamic web serving, and containerized backend microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine configured with 8 vCPUs and 16 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C processors running at 2.7 GHz across 4 physical cores, it includes 105 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. The instance includes no local storage disks and no hardware GPUs, relying on remote persistent disks for block storage. Standardized benchmarks place the instance in the middle tier for general multi-core compute, static web serving throughput at 13.01 GB/sec, and in-memory operations at 8.86 million Redis SET commands per second. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and medium LLM inference show lower performance figures. By reducing memory density to prioritize processing execution, the instance is well suited for CI/CD runners, build automation, web serving, and compute-bound microservice workloads.
